name_reason: Domain part is correct and load-bearing: 'chapter_event_handler' + dispatch idx 0x40 (the per-event handler table @ 0x51B91 is indexed by event idx; verified entry @ 0x51C91 = 0x358EA followed by 0x3599B/idx 0x41 -- sibling handlers _3f/_41/_4a use the same idx convention, so _40 is a real domain ID, NOT address residue). 'unref' is correct (0 direct callers; get_xrefs_to returns only the DATA xref from dispatch table @ 0x51C91). The only mildly imprecise token is the descriptor '_dyn_turn_event': unlike its tail-sharing sibling fd2_chapter_event_handler_4a__ch29_dyn_turn_event (which genuinely schedules the next turn-event by writing tile_event_data_table[+3] = turn_counter+1), THIS handler does not write tile_event_data_table and does not schedule any turn event -- it is a 2-stage dialog/cinematic dispatcher (stage 1: dialog page 1 + 3-portrait white-flash cutscene + battle_anim_phase=1; stage 2: dialog page 2 + mass-kill runtime chars 0x10..end). However '_dyn_turn_event' plausibly denotes membership in the dyn-turn-event handler family that shares the flags[0x10] stage counter and the 0x35992 advance-and-return tail with handler_4a, rather than 'schedules a turn event'. Name is cross-referenced by other plates (handler_4a's plate names 'handler_40 @ 0x358EA'); a descriptor change (e.g. _40__unref_2stage_cutscene) is marginal and would break that family-naming consistency. Left as uncertain for Stage 2 to decide; no address residue, so keep is also defensible.
purpose: Unreferenced chapter event handler (dispatch idx 0x40); a 2-stage state-machine dispatcher that, on its stage counter, plays a dialog+portrait cutscene or a dialog+mass-kill, then advances the stage byte.
logic_summary: Reads stage = (zero-extended byte) tile_event_consumed_flags[0x10]. If stage==1: fd2_display_dialog_scene(current_chapter_text, page=1, ...) then three fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash calls at tiles/ids (9,0x2C,3),(0,9,4),(0x11,9,5), then data_fd2_battle_anim_phase=1. Else if stage==2: fd2_display_dialog_scene(current_chapter_text, page=2, ...) then fd2_kill_runtime_chars_from_index_to_end(0x10) (kills runtime char slots 0x10..end). For any other stage (0 or 3+) the dispatch body is skipped. In all cases the stage byte is then incremented by 1 (8-bit INC) so consecutive calls dispatch in order. In the binary the unconditional advance+return is a Class-3 shared tail at 0x35992 (MOV EAX,[flags_ptr]; INC byte[EAX+0x10]; RET) which this function's own non-stage-1/2 exits JMP to and which fd2_chapter_event_handler_4a also tail-borrows; the source's if/else-if + unconditional increment is functionally exact.

At stage 1 EAX==1 -> source literal page=1 matches; at stage 2 EAX==2 -> source literal page=2 matches.
